overview: The 50 mm controller uses measured state to adjust reference joint and wheel commands. Its final policy combines earlier learned motion with local refinements; retaining a component freezes its weights, not its state-dependent computation.

The latest 100 mm experiment adds a much smaller learning problem: a two-dimensional Gaussian distribution over wheel-compensation gains while keeping the inherited joint policy fixed. It is not a new whole-body neural policy trained from scratch.
Both comparisons evaluate the complete implemented controller. Their results do not isolate PPO learning as the sole cause of the observed difference.
observations_note: The final 50 mm interface contains 536 values. The groups below are semantic categories, not an additive dimension partition: the retained architectures also contain explicit extensions and padded historical fields. Actor and critic receive the same measured vector; no privileged-critic-only split is claimed. These are simulator-derived signals, not evidence of a hardware sensor suite.

observations.details: Body/chassis orientation, projected gravity, roll/pitch, angular rate and acceleration, linear velocity and acceleration.
Eight measured leg-joint positions and velocities, four measured wheel velocities, and nominal/applied target information.
Wheel normal forces and active contacts, load fractions, support count, support validity and geometric margin.
Obstacle planes and wheel geometry relative to the body/step, wheel body velocities, projected CoM information.
Motion phase/substage, elapsed and remaining time, goal features, lift/crossing/placement history and completed stages. Motion phase is observed context, not an action output.

observations.dimensions: 6 × 12 = 72 history values within the larger interface
observations.details: Previous raw request, previous and previous-previous bounded residual, previous and previous-previous applied commands, and previous nominal command. This is explicit finite history, not an LSTM.

architectures.outputs: 12 Gaussian means and separate standard deviations
architectures.training: Historical initialization; distinct from the final 536-value composite interface.

architectures.inputs: 439-value interface at the selected early checkpoint
architectures.network: Two 256-unit ELU hidden layers; retained inside later actors
architectures.training: Learned motion retained with fixed weights during later local refinements.

architectures.inputs: Explicit extended measured-state layouts around the retained predecessor
architectures.network: Two 128-unit ELU hidden layers in the selected local networks
architectures.outputs: 12 residual coordinates with Gaussian exploration after activation
architectures.training: Only the eligible new component learns; the preceding actor continues to execute with frozen weights.

architectures.inputs: Measured eligibility and the retained composite state
architectures.network: One local FL-wheel Gaussian innovation; 2 new actor scalars
architectures.outputs: One eligible FL-wheel correction; other coordinates retained
architectures.training: 2,048 stored decisions = 587 actor-eligible + 1,461 value-only; 4 PPO updates, 80 Adam steps (60 with policy eligibility).

architectures.inputs: No observation input to the learned head; one raw latent pair per episode
architectures.network: 2 learned Gaussian means + 2 learned log standard deviations; no new MLP
architectures.outputs: Sigmoid-transformed RR/RL transfer gains, each bounded to (0,1)
architectures.training: 32 complete simulation episodes; 4 batches; 9 optimizer steps. The inherited joint policy stays fixed.

hyperparameters.fifty: Later local rollout: 512 policy decisions, 1 environment; retained early rollout: 128 decisions.
hyperparameters.hundred: 8 complete episodes per batch; 4 batches (32 episodes).

hyperparameters.fifty: 15 Hz policy; 120 Hz target dispatch and physics.
hyperparameters.hundred: Gain held for the episode; measured eligibility/request refreshed at the existing 15 Hz control step; 120 Hz physical interface.
Up to 5 full-batch epochs; stop early above exact Gaussian KL 0.025.

hyperparameters.fifty: Later local γ = 0.9985; GAE λ = 0.99. Initial early training used 0.995 / 0.95.
hyperparameters.hundred: Standardized complete-episode returns; no critic and no GAE.

hyperparameters.fifty: Adam with adaptive LR, target KL 0.01; saved component snapshots vary.
hyperparameters.hundred: Adam, LR 0.08; four trainable scalar parameters.
Not applicable to the context-free new head.

hyperparameters.fifty: Selected deterministic policy; no online updates.
hyperparameters.hundred: Deterministic sigmoid of Gaussian mean; no sampling or further learning.

hyperparameters_note: Do not present all 50 mm ancestry as one stationary run: observation layouts, rewards, rollout settings and adaptive learning rates changed. The 100 mm episodic update must not inherit the 50 mm critic/GAE description.
learning_rates_note: These are checkpoint optimizer snapshots from an adaptive schedule, not constant learning rates over the full run.

rewards.terms: Task progress with evolving secondary body/contact/smoothness preferences; later limited front-body quality weights 0.03 and 0.06.
rewards.caveat: The objective changed during development, so the stages do not form one stationary learning curve.

rewards.terms: Potential shaping 5(γΦ_next − Φ_current); RR contact +10, RL lift +10, RL crossing +15, RL placement +20; completion +80, failure −40, time cost 0.02/s.
rewards.caveat: A wheel-contact milestone is not task completion.

rewards.terms: A stage-specific potential for front preparation, support transfer and continued rear-left progress; completion/failure and elapsed-time terms retained.
rewards.caveat: Earlier potential values may remain diagnostic; the active objective is stage-specific.

rewards.terms: Forward displacement +5/m; reverse-final-command and loaded counterdrive costs of 0.1/s each in the eligible interval; inherited completion return.
rewards.caveat: The optimized return is the eligible FL-window total. Off-window rows can contribute to value estimation without an actor update.

rewards.terms: Terminal completion tier minus bounded tilt-RMS, peak-tilt and support costs; limited lift-progress bonus only when neither success rule passes.
rewards.caveat: Uses complete-episode metrics during training. Published paired RMS comparisons use the separately identified geometric-completion window.

request_caps50.channel_order: FL hip, FL knee, FR hip, FR knee, RL hip, RL knee, RR hip, RR knee; then FL, FR, RL, RR wheels.
request_caps50.note: Symmetric signed request caps in the accepted final 50 mm profile, before state-dependent feasibility, slew and actuator limits. They are not standard deviations, final motor targets, or the caps used by every historical ancestor. Motion phases P01–P13 are execution states, not the four learning stages.

head100.title: What the latest 100 mm update actually learns
head100.description: The new head learns a distribution over two episode-level wheel-progress gains, one for each rear-wheel transfer period. It leaves the inherited joint policy unchanged. At evaluation the gains are fixed, while the applied correction still changes with measured contact, clearance and remaining geometric deficit.
head100.raw_std_note: Raw dimensionless training-distribution parameters. Evaluation uses the means; these are not actuator noise or wheel-speed limits.
head100.mapping: An eligible transfer produces a shared additive request on all four equally commanded forward-rolling wheels. The amplitude is gain × 0.15 rad/s × clipped remaining-deficit fraction. It decays to zero as the rear wheel clears the front boundary, and the original wheel-speed limit still applies.
head100.mapping_caveat: These two gains do not independently command the two rear wheel motors. This is the new learned update, not the complete controller.
head100.eligibility_summary: Measured airborne rear-wheel clearance, supporting contacts and support qualification gate the request. Stop, zero/reverse or unequal nominal wheel commands bypass it.
head100.selection: Require both common and native success on the nominal condition; rank eligible development candidates by strict completion, then common completion and fewer collision aborts; use paired posture as a tie-break. Freeze the checkpoint before evaluating held-out cases.

equations.explanation: The raw 50 mm Gaussian request z is mapped into a signed physical request. C is a phase-specific cap: degrees for joints, rad/s for wheels. Subsequent feasibility, coordination and actuator constraints produce the final target.

equations.formula: L_clip(θ) = E[min(ρ A, clip(ρ, 1−ε, 1+ε) A)], ρ = π_θ / π_old, ε = 0.2
equations.explanation: PPO clips the probability-ratio update, not the physical motor command. The 50 mm advantage uses a value estimate and GAE; the new 100 mm head instead uses standardized whole-episode returns.

equations.formula: z ~ N(μ, diag(σ²)); g = sigmoid(z); g_eval = sigmoid(μ)
equations.explanation: One joint 2D latent sample produces the two gains for a complete training episode. The policy has two means and two log-standard-deviation parameters; deterministic evaluation uses only the means.

d_j is the remaining rear-wheel-center distance to the obstacle front plus wheel radius and 5 mm clearance, in metres. The eligible rear transfer selects j; the same extra canonical speed is added to all four forward wheel targets subject to the original limit.

equations.formula: R = B − 20 a/(a+12°) − 10 p/(p+30°) − 5 min(T_bad/T,1) + b_progress
equations.explanation: a and p are full-episode tilt RMS and peak tilt. T_bad includes support-unknown and negative-margin duration. B is +120 when both success rules pass, −20 when exactly one passes, and −100 when neither passes. b_progress is 0–4 and only applies when neither rule passes. The disjoint episode tiers prioritize completion, but optimizing expected reward is not a formal lexicographic guarantee.
